A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SubTrack++ by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reorganization and additional material in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original C4 pre-training, GLUE and SuperGLUE fine-tuning, component ablations, runtime measurements, and Ackley-function experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds longer pre-training, sensitivity and gradient-norm analyses, and Alpaca fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: Equation (5), Algorithm 1, and the update restated in Section 3 change the sine term from positive to negative. v3 explicitly follows the negative gradient, correcting the specified update direction while retaining all three method components. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds supervised instruction fine-tuning of Llama-2-7B-chat-hf on Alpaca. C4, GLUE, SuperGLUE, and the Ackley test are retained; the longer C4 run changes training duration rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding pre-training and fine-tuning comparisons retain their baseline membership, including APOLLO and GoLore in the multi-baseline plots. The new long-training and Alpaca comparisons use the already evaluated GaLore baseline. Newly discussed LoRA done RITE and LORO are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported pre-training SubTrack++ step size changes from 10 to 10000 (v2 Table 10; v3 Table 4). Fine-tuning step sizes also change: SST-2 from 0.01 to 0.1, CB from 1 to 10, and COPA from 50 to 10. v3 adds update-rank/frequency sweeps, one-epoch Alpaca evaluation, and a stated 100k-iteration 7B run. Figure 7's Step axis nevertheless extends to 400k, leaving its counting convention unclear. These disclosures do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and Ackley experiment, v3 adds update-frequency and update-rank sensitivity tests (Figure 5), longer-training convergence analysis (Figure 7), full versus projected gradient-norm tracking on Llama-1B, and tangent-norm tracking on Llama-350M. These substantially expand evidence about stability and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions report results without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's checklist explicitly acknowledges that statistical testing was infeasible, but introduces no uncertainty estimates or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes SubTrack++ losses for 1B/3B/7B from 4.51/4.49/4.62 to 4.52/4.50/4.63. Fine-tuning results also change, including RTE 76.53 to 78.34 and CB 89.66 to 83.96; reported setting revisions prevent treating all changes as same-setting gains. New results include long-training losses of 3.37 versus GaLore's 4.64 and Alpaca perplexities of 2.41 versus 2.43, with runtimes of 73.2 versus 110.8 minutes. Existing pre-training memory and runtime tables retain their values.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the mathematical application of the Grassmann exponential to descent, introducing the negative sine term and explicitly identifying the negative-gradient direction. The convergence assumptions, theorem statements, and proofs and optimizer derivations in Appendices A–C are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The central three-component method and efficiency claims remain. The abstract replaces the 43% pre-training time reduction on a 1B model with claims of up to 65% pre-training and 36% fine-tuning reductions. The latter percentage is inconsistent with Table 9, whose times imply approximately 34%.

C2.justification: v3 adds implicit regularization as an explanation for outperforming full-rank training, interprets gradient-norm tracking as evidence of full-gradient convergence, and explains instability under excessive update frequency or rank. It newly acknowledges the absence of statistical testing. Existing fixed-subspace theory caveats and limitations concerning non-Adam optimizers and models above 7B remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository pointer and Alpaca implementation details, including an H100 GPU, batch size 8, rank 1024, and attention/MLP target modules. It revises the step-size tables and specifies that the longer pre-training run otherwise follows Table 4's settings.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds discussions of LoRA done RITE and LORO. v3 removes four Rajabi–Rambhatla workshop references and some background citations, while adding benchmark references. Its new SuperGLUE citation points to Sarlin et al.'s feature-matching paper, which does not match the reported NLP benchmark tasks.

P1.justification: Introduction and method paragraphs are shortened or rephrased, and experimental explanations are expanded. The pre-training and fine-tuning appendices exchange positions, redundant Appendix H is absorbed into existing discussion, and acknowledgments and a checklist are added. The main six-section narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 combines v2 Figures 3 and 6 into the two-panel component ablation in Figure 4, redraws comparison plots, and adds sensitivity and long-training figures. Figure 8 redisplays Figure 1 as labeled bars. New Alpaca result and hyperparameter tables accompany substantial table relocation and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The descent-sign correction improves the published algorithm's correctness, while targeted stability analyses, longer training, and instruction fine-tuning strengthen empirical support beyond v2. These gains are limited by unexplained parameter revisions and reporting inconsistencies, including Figure 7's iteration labeling and the fine-tuning speedup percentage. Statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
